title: Melanophore Response Assay in Zebrafish
author: Caio Maximino
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.qf7dtrn

steps.title: Anesthetize zebrafish
steps.instruction: Anesthetize fish by immersion in eugenol (60-100 ppm) in a 50 ml beaker using Methyl eugenol (Biorbyt Catalog #orb105046).

steps.title: Position fish for imaging
steps.instruction: Transfer the anesthetized animal to a 90 x 15 cm glass Petri dish under a dissection microscope.

substeps.instruction: Ensure the Petri dish contains enough eugenol solution to cover the animal's body to keep it alive.
Use tweezers to position the animal on its side so the dorsal portion of the body is visible.

steps.title: Capture and prepare image
steps.instruction: Take a still photo of the fish and export it in a format readable by ImageJ.

steps.title: Process image in FIJI ImageJ
steps.instruction: Open the image file in FIJI ImageJ and convert it to 8-bit (Image > Type > 8-bit).

steps.title: Apply Auto Local Threshold
steps.instruction: Transform the image into black and white using the Auto Local Threshold tool (Image > Adjust > Auto Local Threshold).

substeps.instruction: Select the Phansalkar method for thresholding.
Tick the 'White objects of black background' box.

steps.title: Crop melanophore region
steps.instruction: Select and crop the image to isolate the target melanophores.

substeps.instruction: Use the polygon tool to make a selection involving the majority of melanophores in the third strip (from most dorsal to most ventral).

steps.title: Analyze particles
steps.instruction: Apply the Analyze Particles plugin (Analyze > Analyze Particles) with specific filters and settings.

substeps.instruction: Tick 'Summarize', 'Exclude on edges', and 'In situ show'.
Untick all other boxes and click OK.

steps.title: Repeat and summarize data
steps.instruction: Repeat the protocol for each image.

substeps.instruction: If using multiple still photos from the same animal, summarize data as an average value per animal before statistical analysis to prevent pseudoreplication.
